items.title: Bytes survive option, environment, command-block and guard-output paths
accept: set -g @x a\376b (argv or source-file -) stores the bytes; show-options -g @x prints a\376b as the pin does, and #{@x} expands to the same bytes as the pin for UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 clients.
A registry item records the divergence first if the store change is split across commits, and closes with it.
Sourcing `if-shell -F 1 { set-buffer -b x a<fe>b }` stores 61 fe 62 as tmux 3.8 does (zz stores 61 ef bf bd 62: command blocks are reparsed through a lossy string view).

X=a<fd>b in one sourced file then set-buffer -b y "$X" in another stores 61 fd 62 as 3.8 does (the second file takes the text-only parse path and reads the lossy global_environment_variable accessor).

A UTF-8 control client gets raw bytes for an inserted or sourced show-buffer as 3.8 does (ControlCommandGuard.output is a String in the protocol today; changing it is a wire append under the unreleased version).

items.title: Floating panes in the mux and daemon

In [A, (B / C)], break-pane -W -t A then join-pane -s A -t A restores A beside the whole B/C column with 3.8's geometry.
Every error string in the design's commands table answers verbatim.

Zoom: after resize-pane -Z on a tile, new-pane -A keeps window_zoomed_flag 1 with the float in window_visible_layout; a plain new-pane from that over-zoom float keeps the window zoomed on the new pane; a plain new-pane from a tile unzooms; killing the -A float keeps the zoom; resize-pane -Z on a 20x6 float gives it the window's size and unzoom gives back 20x6; all as 3.8.

Modal: after new-pane -O, select-pane elsewhere keeps it active, break-pane/join-pane/swap-pane answer 'pane is modal', a second -O errors, killing it restores the previous pane, killing the previous pane first makes the close fall back as window_lost_pane does; window_modal_pane and window flag O match 3.8.
select-layout with each window_layout string from the scenario restores the same tree and floats.

No tiled pane: break-pane -W of the sole tile, its kill, and a plain break-pane or join-pane of it into another window each leave a window of floats whose list-panes and window_layout match 3.8; a self join-pane there tiles the float to the whole window; the window closes with its last pane; the snapshot carries LayoutNode::Empty.

Daemon tests: with two attached clients, display-popup -E 'sleep 1' puts one modal in both snapshots, sends no EventPayload::Popup, and closes on exit; from a command client display-popup -E 'exit 3' exits 3; display-popup -C kills a new-pane -O modal; a second display-popup leaves the pane count alone; display-popup "" runs default-command (or the shell) in a live modal, not an empty pane; no u64::MAX pane id remains in crates/zz-daemon/src.
PTY sizes follow the allocation rule (float, zoomed float, hidden float, clamp), and a client size report for a float changes nothing.
A round-trip test pins the appended snapshot, delta, LayoutNode::Empty and MouseKey.press encodings; one move-pane -X emits exactly one TreeOp::WindowLayout.
